answer: Each agent maintains a unique sable-bound sequential proof chain rooted at a public wharf of random epoch seeds. A probe challenge injects a dune of memory-hard steps that must be traversed sequentially, embedding the agent's prior unique fingerprint so clones cannot share state. An attacker with N identities must tend N independent chains, each requiring 20 sequential minutes of non-parallelizable compute plus 4GB RAM that cannot be pooled; cost scales linearly with N. Checked by hashing the final tip against the expected fingerprint. Matching tips across identities triggers joint slash.
